item.title: U.S. transportation secretary refuses to apologize for FAA's nationwide ground stop
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Aircrafts are seen on the tarmac at John F. Kennedy International Airport in Queens, New York, the United States on Nov. 13, 2026. The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday evening after hours of disruption affected thousands of flights across the country. (Photo by Ziyu Julian Zhu/Xinhua)
WASHINGTON, Nov. 15 (Xinhua) -- U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Sunday refused to apologize for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)'s nationwide ground stop that lasted for hours on Friday, which disrupted over 10,000 flights, with the impact continuing throughout the weekend.
"It happened on my watch," Duffy told NBC News' "Meet the Press." "But I can't apologize for what was passed off to us, and I can't blame Republicans or Democrats because it's all of them."
The transportation secretary blamed his predecessors and previous administrations for failing to do enough to modernize the U.S. air traffic control system, describing it as "30 years of a lack of investment."
Duffy's remarks came two days after the FAA issued a national ground stop that lasted more than four hours, triggering widespread flight cancellations and delays that continued through the weekend. More than 14,000 flights were canceled on Friday and Saturday, according to data from flight-tracking website FlightAware.
U.S. media described the incident as the longest nationwide ground stop since the 9/11 terrorist attacks.
At a press conference on Saturday, Duffy attributed the disruption to "routine maintenance" at a "remote FAA location," where a contractor identified as L3Harris was replacing aging copper wiring with fiber-optic lines.
Duffy has repeatedly urged the U.S. Congress to approve billions of dollars in funding to overhaul the nation's aging air traffic control infrastructure.
At the same press conference, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford offered a "sincere apology to the American traveling public" affected by Friday's nationwide ground stop, emphasizing that the decision to pause all flights was made "out of an abundance of caution."
Bedford said that U.S. air travel was not expected to return to normal schedules until late Sunday.

item.title: Xi's article on jointly building Asia-Pacific community with shared future to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on jointly building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future will be published on Monday.
The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 22nd issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. It is a compilation of excerpts from Xi's important remarks on the subject made between October 2013 and November 2025.
The article stresses that the Asia-Pacific at present is an economic region with the world's greatest growth dynamism and development potential and is widely recognized as an important engine of global economic growth.
It calls for sustaining the region's strong development momentum, embracing a future of shared prosperity and jointly building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future featuring openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven growth, greater connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation.
The article points out that the Asia-Pacific should remain the locomotive of economic globalization. Efforts should be made to contribute significantly to the world through more vibrant and resilient Asia-Pacific cooperation, it notes.
The article calls for taking the lead in safeguarding peace and stability, and resolving differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation.
It emphasizes the need to play a leading role in enhancing openness and connectivity, firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, and advance regional economic integration and the building of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific.
The article also urges efforts to lead the way in pursuing win-win cooperation, fostering a pattern of cooperation in which countries support each other's success and achieve common development.
It further underlines the importance of taking the lead in pursuing benefits for all and inclusiveness, with efforts to better bridge development gaps, continuously improve people's well-being, and advance common prosperity for all people in the Asia-Pacific.
The article stresses that no matter how far China develops, it will remain rooted in the Asia-Pacific, contribute to its development and bring benefits to the region. China will remain committed to the path of peaceful development and pursue a win-win strategy of opening up. While pursuing its own development, China will actively promote common development among Asia-Pacific countries and create more opportunities for people in the region, it states.
The article says China stands ready to work with all parties to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, promote regional growth and prosperity, and advance practical cooperation in areas that include the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, connectivity, the digital economy and artificial intelligence.

item.title: APEC comes to Shenzhen: where "China Opportunity 2.0" meets the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
This photo taken on Nov. 13, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)
BEIJING, Nov. 15 (Xinhua) -- Next week, the gaze of the Asia-Pacific will turn to a young metropolis in southern China that, about four decades ago, was little more than a quiet fishing village.
Shenzhen will play host to the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting -- the first time in 12 years that China has hosted the top event of the region's highest-level, most extensive and most influential economic cooperation mechanism.
China officially joined APEC in 1991. Shenzhen, adjacent to Hong Kong, will become the third Chinese city after Shanghai and Beijing to welcome this gathering.
Its rise over the past few decades stands as a miracle in the annals of global development, demonstrating what the Chinese people can achieve.
When Shenzhen was designated a special economic zone in 1980, its GDP stood at just 270 million yuan (around 40.2 million U.S. dollars). By 2025, that figure had soared to 3.87 trillion yuan, trailing only Shanghai and Beijing.
China's choice of Shenzhen mirrors a pattern common to other APEC economies, which tend to favor national capitals, major economic or technological hubs, or internationally renowned tourist destinations as host cities.
For the 2026 APEC "China Year," China has set openness, innovation and cooperation as its three priorities. They echo the very forces that have shaped Shenzhen's development: openness is the city's defining feature, innovation its greatest strength, and cooperation a driving force behind its continued growth.
An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 20, 2026 shows a cargo ship sailing toward Yantian Port in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua)
MARKET FOR THE WORLD
Shenzhen's rise over more than forty years owes much to China's reform and opening up. One of the country's first special economic zones, Shenzhen has been a city of opportunity from the very beginning, pioneering one move after another.
Countless entrepreneurs and innovators have gone there to pursue their ambitions, international investors have established a presence, and Chinese companies such as BYD and Huawei have grown from local businesses into global players.
Shenzhen's tale has unfolded in step with the country's opening up. Today, China is expanding high-standard opening up. It has granted zero-tariff treatment to 63 countries, while remaining the world's second-largest importer for 17 consecutive years.
In recent years, alongside further opening up the flow of goods, services, capital and talent, China has steadily expanded institutional opening up -- a key hallmark of high-standard opening up -- with respect to rules, regulations, management, and standards.
The aim is to build a business environment that is transparent, stable and predictable, and to bring China's institutional framework into closer alignment with international standards.
Shenzhen is a core city in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Under "one country, two systems," the area's distinctive environment of three customs territories and three currencies has created valuable opportunities to explore the alignment of legal rules, cross-border professional practice, mutual recognition of qualifications, streamlined customs clearance and common standards.
In this sense, the area serves as a testing ground for bridging different systems and improving institutional connectivity across the Asia-Pacific.
This photo taken on Nov. 11, 2026 shows a coffee service area at the media center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Mao Siqian)
INNOVATION DIVIDENDS
Today's Shenzhen is internationally known for its technological prowess and is often dubbed "China's Silicon Valley."
It now boasts more than 2 million professionals in science and technology. Yet when the special economic zone was first established in 1980, the city's entire pool of technical personnel consisted of just two people: a tractor mechanic and a veterinarian.
This contrast captures the scale of Shenzhen's transformation. In recent years, Shenzhen's output of new energy vehicles, industrial robots and civilian drones has maintained double-digit growth for extended periods.
The city has also become a popular destination for shoppers and technology enthusiasts looking to scour Huaqiangbei, its famed electronics market, for the latest products and cutting-edge innovations.
China's industrial strengths in emerging sectors such as renewable energy and electric vehicles are no accident. They are the result of years of technological accumulation, well-developed industrial supply chains, and the opportunities created by a vast domestic market.
If the "China Opportunity 1.0" of the past was largely about offering the world market dividends via China's enormous consumer market and low-cost production factors, today's "China Opportunity 2.0" is about delivering even greater market dividends while generating innovation dividends through technological progress and industrial upgrading.
In China, businesses from around the world can quickly find partners to work with across the entire process, from research and development and prototype testing to mass production. Companies can tap into the Chinese market while strengthening their competitiveness in global markets.
Seeing these advantages, foreign companies have increasingly moved beyond simply selling their products in China in recent years. Many have also established research and development centers and regional headquarters in the country.
In 2025, 14,000 new foreign-invested enterprises were established in China's scientific research and technical services sector, a year-on-year increase of 27.2 percent.
This photo taken on Nov. 3, 2026 shows a view of Shennan Avenue in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)
COOPERATION FOR SHARED PROSPERITY
The ocean connects rather than divides. Linked by the Pacific, the Asia-Pacific is one of the world's most dynamic economic regions, with deeply integrated regional economies and closely interconnected industrial and supply chains.
Cooperation underpins the shared prosperity of the Asia-Pacific and is essential to building an Asia-Pacific community. Against a backdrop of rising unilateralism and protectionism, one of China's most important responsibilities as APEC host is to help bring economies back to the path of openness and cooperation.
With global challenges -- climate change, food and energy security, demographic shifts and development imbalances -- intertwined and compounding, no single economy can prosper alone.
Over the past year, the 2026 APEC "China Year" has produced substantial results. Working with other APEC member economies, China has organized more than 300 APEC meetings and events, which covered a wide range of areas, including trade, tourism, small and medium-sized enterprises, and energy. They helped build consensus on a series of areas for cooperation.
Next week in Shenzhen, participating economies are expected to build on that consensus and deliver more practical outcomes in key areas such as trade, connectivity, the digital economy and artificial intelligence.
Such progress would provide fresh impetus for economic growth and prosperity across the Asia-Pacific and beyond.

item.title: China's railway network handles record 4.13 billion passenger trips in first 10 months of 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Arriving passengers are pictured at Nanjing Railway Station in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 7, 2026. (Photo by Su Yang/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's railway network handled 4.13 billion passenger trips in the first 10 months of the year, up 4.7 percent year on year and the highest for the period on record, China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway) said on Saturday.
The rise reflects increased capacity, improved services and stronger support for tourism and international passenger services.
During the January-October period, the railway operator ran an average of 11,670 passenger trains per day, up 5 percent year on year, according to the company.
Both passenger trips and passenger transport capacity hit single-day records on Oct. 1, the first day of the National Day holiday, with 25.2 million passenger trips recorded and 14,885 trains operated.
Beyond regular passenger services, railway authorities have been promoting the integration of rail and tourism. In the first 10 months of 2026, 3,236 dedicated tourism trains were operated, while an additional 1,084 special trains were arranged for concerts, sports events, exhibitions and study tours.
These efforts are part of a broader drive to stimulate service consumption and support local economies along rail corridors.
Cross-border passenger services also grew strongly in the period. The Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed railway carried 29.23 million cross-border passengers, up 11 percent year on year, while the China-Laos Railway handled 289,000 cross-border passengers, up 33 percent.
China's railways also saw a surge in foreign visitors. A total of 22.52 million foreign passenger trips were made on the national rail network in the first 10 months of 2026, up 32.9 percent year on year, as more international travelers opted to "tour China by train."
Official data showed that by the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country.

item.title: China's independently developed 10-tonne electric aircraft completes first piloted flight
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
This photo taken on Nov. 14, 2026 shows the 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft CE-25A during its maiden piloted flight in Binzhou, east China's Shandong Province. China's independently developed 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft CE-25A completed its maiden piloted flight on Saturday, according to the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC). The aircraft carried two pilots and one flight-test engineer during the flight in Binzhou, east China's Shandong Province. The CE-25A is COMAC's first electric commercial aircraft. Designed mainly for intercity commercial flights, it can carry 19 passengers and has a maximum takeoff weight of 10 tonnes. It has a cruising speed of 300 km per hour, a cruising altitude of 2,400 meters and a range of 400 km. (Photo by Wang Jiliang/Xinhua)
SHANGHAI, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's independently developed 10-tonne electric commercial aircraft CE-25A completed its maiden piloted flight on Saturday, according to the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC).
The aircraft carried two pilots and one flight-test engineer during the flight in Binzhou, east China's Shandong Province. The aircraft operated normally, and all performance indicators met expectations, COMAC said.
The aircraft completed its first unmanned autonomous flight on Feb. 2 this year.
Developed jointly by COMAC, Chinese battery maker CATL, Shanghai Jiao Tong University and other partners, the CE-25A has completed 19 unmanned autonomous flight validations.
The Civil Aviation Administration of China has accepted COMAC's application for a type certificate.

item.title: How Xi's three visits to Shenzhen show China's commitment to reform and opening up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to attend the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, in south China's Guangdong Province, marking his fourth visit to the birthplace of the country's market-based reforms.
Selected in the late 1970s as a testing ground for China's transition to a more open and market-driven economy, Shenzhen benefited from its proximity to Hong Kong and Macao and its access to maritime trade routes. It has since transformed from a small fishing village into a key driver of China's economic development.
Over the years, Xi has made three visits to Shenzhen. Though each of his visits came at a different stage of the city's and the nation's development, they shared a common thread: China's commitment to pressing ahead with reform and opening up.
Chinese President Xi Jinping places a floral tribute at the bronze statue of Deng Xiaoping in Lianhuashan Park, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, China, on October 14, 2012. /Xinhua
2012: the first inspection tour
Spearheaded by former Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, reform and opening up marked a watershed moment that fundamentally reshaped China's economic and social fabric.
Launched in December 1978, the policy steered the country away from a centrally planned economy toward a market-oriented system, unleashing entrepreneurial energy and igniting a nationwide economic boom.
Much has been achieved. In 1978, China's gross domestic product (GDP) was 367.9 billion yuan, or $149.5 billion, according to World Bank data, which is also cited by the National Bureau of Statistics of China. In just under 50 years, China has developed into the world's second-largest economy, with its GDP reaching 140.19 trillion yuan ($20.4 trillion).
Recognizing the role of reform and opening up in driving this transformation, Xi has repeatedly emphasized the need to uphold and carry forward its legacy. In December 2012, just a month after Xi became the general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, he chose Shenzhen as the first stop of his inspection tour.
During this visit, Xi laid a floral tribute at the bronze statue of Deng Xiaoping in Lianhuashan Park and planted a banyan tree, a symbol of vitality and resilience, underscoring China's dedication to economic reform and determination to navigate any headwinds along the way.
Reaffirming his resolve to stay the course, Xi said, "The decision to launch reform and opening up was right. We must keep to this correct path." He added, "We must stay unwavering on the road to the prosperity of the nation and the people."
Chinese President Xi Jinping visits an exhibition on Guangdong's 40 years of development since the country's reform and opening up, at a museum in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, October 24, 2018. /Xinhua
2018: 40th anniversary of reform and opening up
In October 2018, Xi returned to Shenzhen as the nation marked the 40th anniversary of its reform and opening up, a trip that signaled continued commitment to the policy and an emphasis on greater integration with the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA).
"I come to visit Shenzhen as it marks the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up to tell the world that China will not stop its reform and opening up. China will certainly deliver a bigger miracle that draws worldwide attention," he said.
During his visit, Xi urged the city to deepen cooperation with neighboring Hong Kong to play a bigger role in building the Belt and Road, to advance the development of the GBA, and to participate in international cooperation at higher levels.
In the wake of the visit, China issued the Outline Development Plan for the GBA as well as guidelines to build Shenzhen into a pilot demonstration area of socialism with Chinese characteristics, giving fresh momentum to reform and opening up by laying out a clear path for regional integration.
Chinese President Xi Jinping takes in the view of Shenzhen at Lianhuashan Park, Guangdong Province, China, October 14, 2020. /Xinhua
2020 visit: 40th anniversary of SEZ
During his third visit in 2020, Xi returned to Shenzhen to attend a grand gathering marking the 40th anniversary of the establishment of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone (SEZ).
The occasion came at a critical juncture in China's development, as the country faced mounting domestic and external economic pressures. Yet its stance on reform and opening up remained firm.
Addressing the gathering, Xi said, "The world economy is currently facing complicated challenges. By no means should we be stopped by the reversing trends and tides. We should choose the right side of the history to unswervingly expand opening-up in an all-round way, and promote the building of an open world economy and the building of a community with a shared future for humanity."
China's resolve in implementing reform and opening up has yielded significant results over the years. In the first three quarters of 2026, Shenzhen's GDP exceeded 3.02 trillion yuan, marking a 6.0% year-on-year increase at constant prices, an achievement that would not have been possible without the choices made decades ago.
Hailing the policy as the key to China's astonishing development during his 2021 speech marking the Communist Party of China's (CPC) centenary, Xi stressed that reform and opening up was a crucial move in making China what it is today, demonstrating once again the Party's commitment to the policy and its steady leadership.
In November 1991, China officially joined APEC, marking a major milestone in its reform and opening up policy by deepening its integration into the regional economy and expanding multilateral trade.
Thirty-five years later, China is bringing APEC to Shenzhen, the very place where its nationwide opening up to the world began. Coming full circle, China is once again rolling out the red carpet for the world.

item.title: How China is rebuilding 3,000-year-old bronze treasures
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
How do you put ancient treasures back together after thousands of years? At China's Sanxingdui archaeological site, conservators combine meticulous hands-on restoration with 3D scanning and digital modeling to study broken bronze artifacts and help reveal the extraordinary craftsmanship of ancient Shu civilization.
